== History ==
The founding era is unknown. According to 'History of Kawanishi City,' this area was formerly called "Kawabe District Ōmiwa-gō," and it is said that a ritual group from {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}} (the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miwa clan}}) migrated here and founded the shrine by enshrining their ancestor {{ill|Ōtataneko|fr|Ōtataneko|ja|大田田根子|qid=Q55536798|lt=Ōtataneko-no-Mikoto}} or {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}. When the current enshrined deities were adopted is unknown, but tradition says they were invited from the deities of {{ill|Hirano Shrine|arz|هيرانو جينجا|de|Hirano-Schrein|es|Santuario Hirano|fr|Hirano-jinja|ja|平野神社|ru|Хирано-дзиндзя|zh|平野神社|qid=Q738971}} when {{ill|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|ast|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|es|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|fa|میناموتو نو میتسوناکا|fr|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|it|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|ja|源満仲|ko|미나모토노 미쓰나카|oc|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|pt|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|sv|Minamoto no Mitsunaka|zh|源滿仲|qid=Q2531241}} made {{ill|Tada-no-shō|ja|多田荘|qid=Q24859505}} his base.

After the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ar|ميناموتو (عشيرة)|ca|Clan Minamoto|ckb|بنەماڵەی مینامۆتۆ|de|Minamoto|eo|Minamoto (klano)|es|Clan Minamoto|et|Minamoto|eu|Minamoto klana|fa|خاندان میناموتو|fi|Minamoto-klaani|fr|Clan Minamoto|he|שבט מינאמוטו|hu|Minamoto család|id|Klan Minamoto|it|Clan Minamoto|ja|源氏|ka|მინამოტო|ko|미나모토씨|ms|Suku Minamoto|nl|Minamoto|no|Minamoto|pa|ਮਿਨਾਮੋਤਾ|pl|Minamoto (ród)|pt|Clã Minamoto|ru|Минамото|sh|Minamoto (klan)|simple|Minamoto clan|sr|Клан Минамото|sv|Minamoto|ta|மினாமோட்டோ குலம்|th|ตระกูลมินาโมโตะ|tr|Minamoto boyu|uk|Мінамото|vi|Gia tộc Minamoto|zh|源氏|zh_min_nan|Minamoto--sī|qid=Q599881}} made Tada-no-shō their base, the shrine stood in the northeast direction from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadain}}, their residence, and was treated as a guardian deity and called "Hirano Myōjin"; it was known by this name through early modern times<ref>Sadatoshi Yoshii, "Shikinaisha Survey Report Vol. 5" (1977) {{全国書誌番号|78005760}}</ref>.
